findings.title: meas-two-run genuinely rejects byte-identical duplicates and disagreement
findings.detail: Live-ran meas-two-run.mjs against az-planting-calendar's real evidence (clean pass). Then hand-mutated a scratch copy of evidence/measurement-meta.json: (1) duplicated fe-search-present's first run object verbatim as both entries -> meas-two-run correctly FAILed with 'the two recorded runs are byte-identical'; (2) set the two runs to {ok:true} and {ok:false} -> correctly FAILed with 'two runs disagree'. Both directions hold.

findings.title: Six fe-* browser checks run two genuinely independent full passes, timestamped on completion
findings.citation: fe-light-dark.mjs:523-526, fe-search-present.mjs:789-792, fe-breadcrumbs.mjs:567-570, fe-brand-mark-size.mjs:387-390, fe-result-in-viewport.mjs:569-572, fe-resource-links.mjs:567-575
findings.detail: Read each run1/run2 construction: every one opens a fresh page (or fresh crawl) per pass, navigates fresh, and captures nowIso() only after that pass's await resolves -- not two clock reads back-to-back on one computed value. Live-ran fe-light-dark against all four orchestrator/test/fixtures/theme-paint/*.html fixtures: gradient-shell-changes.html PASS, gradient-shell-unchanged.html FAIL, hardcoded-hero.html (known-bad) FAIL, tokenised.html PASS -- real Playwright renders, not fixture text-matching. fe-resource-links.mjs:513-514 shares one Map across both crawls, but only for external-URL-liveness memoization (documented at :507-512); each crawl still opens its own page and re-discovers links from a fresh DOM. This is a defensible optimization (avoids doubling real network calls to the same third-party host), not the vacuous 'one result written twice' pattern the original review flagged -- reviewed and not counted as a defect.

findings.title: meas-known-bad: prose/typo paths correctly fail, but a MISSING or empty knownBad.input silently skips the rerun proof entirely
findings.detail: Confirmed live that the original defect (prose or a typo'd path satisfying G1) is fixed: ran meas-known-bad.mjs against az-planting-calendar's real evidence with knownBad.input mutated to 'a fixture with a dead search box' and to 'nonexistent/typo/path.html' in isolated scratch copies -- both correctly exited 1. BUT line 162, `if (typeof kb.input !== 'string' || kb.input.length === 0) continue;`, means an entry that omits `input` altogether (or sets it to '') skips straight past the rerun requirement with zero failures recorded, as long as `failed:true` and a fresh `recordedAt` are present. Reproduced directly: called evaluateKnownBad() with `{knownBad: {failed:true, recordedAt: <now>}}` (no input key) and got `failures: []` -- G1 passes with no fixture ever having been proven to fail. This is the same class of hole the fix was written to close, just reached by omitting the field instead of writing prose in it. Does not currently affect az-planting-calendar (every rule's measurement-meta.json has a real, resolvable absolute knownBad.input), but the check itself is not sound against a future or careless entry.

findings.title: lg-shipped condition 5: the rules-list exclusion is real, but the circularity survives through the stale finalScore
findings.citation: orchestrator/scripts/checks/lg-shipped.mjs:227-233; .github/scripts/meets_the_bar.mjs:273-282 (scoreBarReasons uses result.finalScore, not a recomputed one); orchestrator/src/gate/score.ts:73-74 (any failing blocker, including lg-shipped itself, zeroes the WHOLE score to 0); orchestrator/src/rubric/rules.ts:247 (lg-shipped is severity:'blocker')
findings.detail: The claimed fix filters `lg-shipped` out of `result.rules` before calling scoreBarReasons, and that filter does work -- verified live that when 3 OTHER real rules were also failing, the message correctly omitted lg-shipped from the 'N rule(s) have passed===false' list. But scoreBarReasons' FIRST check is `result.finalScore < threshold`, and `effectiveResult.finalScore` is copied unchanged from the stored file -- never recomputed from the filtered rule set. Because lg-shipped is a blocker and computeScore() zeroes finalScore to 0 whenever ANY blocker fails (score.ts:73-74), a prior run where lg-shipped was the ONLY failing rule still leaves `finalScore: 0` baked into results/<slug>.json. Reproduced in isolation: built a results.json with every rule passing except lg-shipped (matching what computeScore would actually produce, finalScore:0), called requireGateResultMeetsBar() directly, and it still called io.fail() with 'finalScore 0 is below the finish-line threshold 90' -- lg-shipped citing the effect of its own prior failure, just relocated from the rule-list check to the score check. orchestrator/test/lgShipped.test.ts's own new coverage (around line 392-419) masks this: the test fixture hand-authors `finalScore: 100` alongside `lg-shipped: false`, a combination the real computeScore() can never produce (a failing blocker always yields score 0, never 100). The new unit test is green because it tests an unrealistic input, not because the real gap is closed. Live evidence: running `REDANVIL_PRE_PUSH=1 node lg-shipped.mjs az-planting-calendar` right now (41 unpushed commits, deferred) still fails citing 'finalScore 0 is below the finish-line threshold 90' from the stored results/az-planting-calendar.json.

findings.title: REDANVIL_PRE_PUSH deferral is sound: literal '1' only, hook-only, no CI workflow sets it
findings.detail: Confirmed `process.env.REDANVIL_PRE_PUSH === '1'` (strict equality). Live-ran lg-shipped.mjs three ways: unset -> correctly failed on 41 unpushed commits; set to '1' -> correctly deferred that one condition and proceeded to (a real, unrelated) condition 5 failure; set to the sneaky value 'true' -> correctly still failed on unpushed commits. Grepped .github/workflows/ci.yml and drift.yml for REDANVIL_PRE_PUSH -- zero matches (the one hit in ci.yml:87 is a code comment, not an assignment). Only .githooks/pre-push sets and exports it.

findings.title: fe-assistant-present: the specific literal gaps (bare 'filters'/'SYSTEM_PROMPT', 503-as-infra) are closed, but the underlying regex is still text-matchable by a comment or string literal
findings.detail: Confirmed live: a 503 response from a reachable assistant endpoint is a hard fail, not infra (verifyLiveGrounding returns {ok:false} with no infra flag on non-2xx; runAssistantPresent then calls io.fail, never io.infra, for that case -- reproduced with an injected fetch stub returning HTTP 503). Confirmed the bare words 'filters' and 'SYSTEM_PROMPT' alone no longer satisfy GROUNDS_DATA. Residual gap: the patterns are plain regexes over raw file text, not AST-aware, so a comment ('// env.DB is not actually used here') or a hardcoded fake response containing the substring 'env.DB' anywhere in the file still satisfies assessAssistantEndpoint -- reproduced live with a fabricated handler that returns a hardcoded crop list and calls env.AI.run but never touches a database, decorated with a comment mentioning env.DB; assessAssistantEndpoint returned {ok:true}. This does NOT currently affect az-planting-calendar: grepped functions/api/assistant.ts and confirmed real `env.DB`, `D1Database`, `env.AI.run` and a parameterized `.prepare()` call at lines 233-402, and separately ran fe-assistant-present.mjs live against the deployed app -- it executed the LIVE cross-check (tests/assistant-grounding.json exists and deployUrl is recorded) and passed by matching the assistant's returned crop set against the app's own /api/plantable D1 query for the same half-month, which a stub cannot fake on demand. Recorded as a soundness weakness in the check's general design (would misjudge a different or future app), not a live false-positive here.

findings.title: fe-light-dark detects gradient/background-image paint and still fails a cosmetic-only theme toggle
findings.detail: Live-ran fe-light-dark.mjs --fixture against all four orchestrator/test/fixtures/theme-paint/*.html fixtures (real Playwright chromium launches, not code reading): gradient-shell-changes.html -> PASS (5 regions change paint); gradient-shell-unchanged.html -> FAIL, citing every region's background as 'effectively unchanged between themes' including the gradient-painted shell; hardcoded-hero.html (the known-bad fixture) -> FAIL; tokenised.html -> PASS. Both directions of the requirement hold on real renders.

findings.title: productJudgement.mjs is fail-closed and genuinely wired into isDone(); an unnamed reviewer cannot pass
findings.citation: orchestrator/src/team/productJudgement.mjs:87-92 (independentReviewOk), :152-166 (loadProductJudgement); .github/scripts/meets_the_bar.mjs:601-616 (evaluateApp spreads loadProductJudgement into isDone); orchestrator/src/gate/done.mjs:209-233 (isDone gates on independentReviewOk/qaVisualOk/userRefuseOk)
findings.detail: Live-tested independentReviewOk() in an isolated tmp dir against five cases: no `reviewer` field -> false; blank/whitespace `reviewer` -> false; malformed JSON -> false; file missing entirely -> false; real named reviewer + verdict:'pass' -> true. Confirmed evaluateApp() in meets_the_bar.mjs spreads loadProductJudgement(...) directly into the isDone() opts object (not a dead, uncalled function), and done.mjs itself pushes a blocking reason whenever independentReviewOk/qaVisualOk/userRefuseOk are not explicitly true. This closes the original 'meets_the_bar.mjs never supplies independentReviewOk to isDone' finding for real.

notes: verdict is 'fail'. Of the 8 items asked to be re-verified in refute mode: 5 fully hold (meas-two-run, the six independent-run timestamp fixes, the REDANVIL_PRE_PUSH deferral, fe-light-dark's gradient handling, and productJudgement.mjs's fail-closed wiring). 3 have real, live-reproduced residual gaps: (1) meas-known-bad can still be satisfied with zero fixture proof by omitting knownBad.input rather than writing prose in it; (2) lg-shipped condition 5's circularity is NOT actually closed -- the rules-list exclusion filter was applied, but scoreBarReasons checks the stored finalScore first, and a prior lg-shipped-only failure leaves finalScore permanently pinned at 0 (blockers zero the whole score in score.ts), so the check can still fail citing the effect of its own past verdict; the new unit test for this passes only because it hand-authors an impossible finalScore:100+lg-shipped:false combination that real scoring never produces; (3) fe-assistant-present's GROUNDS_DATA patterns are plain text regexes, satisfiable by a comment or stray string containing 'env.DB' with zero real database access -- az-planting-calendar itself is unaffected because its assistant.ts has real D1 calls and the live cross-check independently verifies it against the deployed app, but the check's general soundness has the same shape of hole as the original defect it was written to close. Used grok-4.5 (session bcaeb150-fd0c-4606-9a1f-761db58dd661) as an independent second judge in genuine refute mode; grok's 4 flagged items (of 8) were each independently reproduced or refuted here rather than taken on its word -- 2 (meas-known-bad, lg-shipped) confirmed as real, 1 (fe-assistant-present) confirmed as real but non-blocking for this app, 1 (fe-resource-links shared cache) investigated and refuted as a defensible optimization, not a defect. Also flagging for the team: this review found the working tree being actively mutated by concurrent teammates (evidence/measurement-meta.json, results/az-planting-calendar.json, evidence/verdicts-az-planting-calendar.json, lg-bindings-bound.mjs, fe-favicon-legible.mjs, new fixture dirs) while it ran; do not treat results/az-planting-calendar.json's exact contents at any single instant during this window as settled until that concurrent work lands. Do not treat this as a pass to unblock push -- fix items 3, 4 and 6's soundness gap (or at minimum add unit tests shaped like the real computeScore/regex-defeat cases above) before the next review pass.
